answers.explanation: Equal volumes of gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules, so 25 cm3 of Y contains Z molecules.
8.0 g of H2 is 4 mol, which gives 4 mol of water, and 4 x 18 = 72.0 g.
The flat section of the heating curve shows the solid melting, which ends at about 3.0 minutes.
The gas starts to condense when it reaches the flat boiling section of the cooling curve, at about 150 C.
Element Z has atomic number 20, which is calcium, a metal.
The diagram shows atoms sharing electrons to form the bond, which is a covalent bond.
Gamma rays are used to destroy cancerous growths by radiotherapy.
The average kinetic energy of gas molecules increases as temperature increases.
Millikan's oil drop experiment determined the charge on the electron.
Having 9 protons and 10 electrons gives a net charge of -1, so the particle is a negative ion.
Molar mass = 2 x 32 = 64, so the atomic mass of X = 64 - 32 = 32.
Aluminium tetraoxosulphate(VI) is used as a coagulant in water purification.
Automobile exhausts release heavy metals such as lead, which pollute the environment.
Phosphorus ignites in air, so it is stored under water to prevent it from catching fire.
Distillation separates a liquid from its dissolved impurities by boiling and recondensing, giving a pure solvent.
Deliquescent substances absorb moisture from the air, so they are used as drying agents.
Pyrogallol absorbs oxygen, which makes up 21% of air, so the volume decrease is 0.21 x 30.00 = 6.30 cm3.
Detergents disperse oil in water, so pouring detergents helps spread and break up the spilt petroleum.
Copper loses electrons and is oxidised, so it acts as a reducing agent.
Two gases combine to form a solid, which reduces the number of gas particles, so entropy decreases.
2.7 g Al is 0.1 mol, which needs 0.3 F = 28950 C; over 7200 s this is a current of about 4 A.
Conductivity depends on the number of ions present, so it decreases as the electrolyte concentration falls.
The enthalpy change is positive at +89 kJ/mol, so 89 kJ of energy is absorbed.
Higher temperature gives molecules more kinetic energy, so they collide more frequently and the rate increases.
In 2NO + O2 to 2NO2, the nitrogen oxidation number rises from +2 to +4.
Removing a product, S, shifts the equilibrium to the right and increases the yield of R.
Ethanoic acid has one replaceable hydrogen ion, so it is monobasic.
M displaces zinc from its salt, so M is more electropositive (more reactive) than zinc.
Hydrogen ions gaining electrons to form hydrogen gas is a reduction reaction.
A negative enthalpy change means heat is released, so the reaction is exothermic.
Each carbon in ethyne is bonded by a triple bond and one single bond, so both carbons are sp hybridised.
In acid solution proteins are broken down by hydrolysis of their peptide bonds.
Fermentation converts sugar into alcohol with the help of yeast enzymes.
Catalytic hydrogenation adds hydrogen across the benzene ring, saturating it to give cyclohexane.
Alkanoic acids react with alkanols in a characteristic esterification reaction.
Chlorine reacts with water in sunlight to give hydrochloric acid and oxygen gas.
But-1-ene and but-2-ene both have formula C4H8 but differ in structure, so they are isomers.
Concentrated sulphuric acid removes water from sugar, so it acts as a dehydrating agent.
Sulphur forms cross-links that bind rubber molecules together during vulcanisation.
Sodium reacts with water to form sodium hydroxide, which makes the solution alkaline.
Alkanals have the general formula RCHO, with a terminal aldehyde group.
Calcium salts burn with a brick-red flame in a flame test.
Sulphur(IV) oxide is denser than air, so it is collected by downward displacement of air.
Glycerol contains three hydroxyl groups, so it is a trihydric alkanol.
Silicon(IV) oxide, which is sand, is the main impurity in iron ore.
Burning a candle produces carbon(IV) oxide and water vapour.
